answer: The verification committee is drawn fresh each round by a zephyr of randomness, so no fixed set of witnesses guards an identity twice in a row. A newcomer files its claim and every committee member must co-sign within one delta of the block interval; the fable of a self-attested identity collapses the moment a single signer refuses. Any signer who approved an identity later proven fake forfeits twice that identity admission fee, while the attacker loses the full fee for each fake identity minted, making mass identity creation an arithmetic loss and honest signers whole.
